content:
Alice Nguyen: quick question — in compare mode, when I toggle quick filters the left panel keeps model X pinned but right switches to default model. Is that expected? steps:
Alice Nguyen: 1) open route analytics -> compare
Alice Nguyen: 2) pin model `redwood-l20` on left
Alice Nguyen: 3) apply quickfilter "error rate > 1%"
Alice Nguyen: observed: left still `redwood-l20`, right fell back to route default (`opt-3b`)
Ben Ortiz: hmm that's not great. I thought compare should keep both sides scoped to the same saved query state
Ben Ortiz: maybe quickfilters mutate the global route state instead of the per-pane state :thinking_face:
Carol Singh: @Ben can you repro? I think we wired quickfilters to the route-level filter store so they're applied globally unless you explicitly save to a pane
Ben Ortiz: repro'ing now
devx-bot: SavedQueryService v2 deployed to prod at 2024-04-09T14:12Z — config: allow_pane_scoped_filters=false
Ben Ortiz: yep confirmed — quickfilters update route filters only
Alice Nguyen: that's surprising. UX expectation from PM/design was pane-isolated until you click "Apply to route". We should align with that
Ethan Park: quick thought: two options
Ethan Park: 1) make quickfilters write to pane-local ephemeral state by default and only bubble to route on explicit save
Ethan Park: 2) keep current global behavior but add clear affordance and toast when you change filters ("Changed route filters — this affects all panes")
Carol Singh: option 1 will affect telemetry and quotas, since rate previews are computed per-route. If panes diverge we need per-pane preview endpoints
Carol Singh: backend would need to accept a `pane_id` or `compare_context` when computing quota/preview
Ben Ortiz: example saved-query payload we currently use:
Ben Ortiz: ```
{
  "route_id": "route_123",
  "filters": [{"field":"status","op":"!=","value":200}],
  "name": "Errors > 0",
  "owner": "team-api"
}
```
Ethan Park: proposal: extend to optional model pins and pane metadata
Ethan Park: ```
{
  "route_id":"route_123",
  "filters":[...],
  "model_pin": {"left":"redwood-l20","right":"opt-3b"},
  "scope":"pane", // values: pane | route
  "name":"Errors + pinned compare"
}
```
Alice Nguyen: that would make saved queries more explicit — but we need to decide defaults for export/import and sharing
Carol Singh: telemetry: we currently sample route-level queries at 0.1% and compute cost preview from aggregated tokens. Pane-scoped queries would double the preview calls unless we dedupe
Carol Singh: suggestion: preview API accept `preview_contexts: [context_obj]` so console can send both panes in one call and backend returns aggregated and per-context previews
Ben Ortiz: implementation complexity OK, but migration risk: older saved queries without model_pin should behave as route-scoped
Ethan Park: UX edgecases: what happens on rollout fallback? If left pane pins a model not available in a region, should we auto-fallback or show warning? Propose immediate toast + fallback selector
Alice Nguyen: can we ship lightweight fix first: make quickfilters pane-ephemeral in UI only (no backend change) so users don't get surprised, then follow up with API changes for saved queries + previews
Carol Singh: +1 to incremental. I'll scope a ticket: frontend ephemeral state + UNSENT telemetry flag so we don't create previews until user clicks "Apply to route" or "Save"
Ben Ortiz: I'll add API sketch for `preview_contexts` and optional `model_pin`. I'll ping infra about quotas cost to ensure preview batching
devx-bot: Ticket created: CONSOLE-5172 "Pane-local quickfilters + preview_contexts API" — assignees: Carol, Ben
Alice Nguyen: awesome — thanks. Can we add microcopy: "Filters here affect only this comparison pane" when in compare mode? reduces surprise
Ethan Park: yup I'll drop that in the PR
Carol Singh: timeline: frontend patch for ephemeral quickfilters end of week, API spec next week, backend change after spec review
Ben Ortiz: noted. Will also add a unit-test asserting saved query without `model_pin` is route-scoped
Alice Nguyen: thanks all :raised_hands:
